post_gain.description: Mid-centered gain transformation applied to the elevation values. This is a non-linear recurve operator centered around the mid elevation (typically 0.5). Increasing the gain pushes values toward the minimum and maximum elevations, creating flatter low/high regions with a steeper transition around the midpoint.
post_gain.label: Gain

post_gamma.description: Standard gamma correction applied to the elevation values. This is a monotonic power-law remapping that shifts emphasis toward low or high elevations, making the overall shape sharper or bulkier without changing its ordering.
post_gamma.label: Gamma

post_inverse.description: Inverts the output values after processing, flipping low and high values across the midrange.
post_inverse.label: Invert Output

post_remap.description: Linearly remaps the output values to a specified target range (default is [0, 1]).
post_remap.label: Remap Range

post_saturate.description: Modifies the amplitude of elevations by first clamping them to a given interval and then scaling them so that the restricted interval matches the original input range. This enhances contrast in elevation variations while maintaining overall structure.
post_saturate.label: Saturation Range

post_smoothing_radius.description: Defines the radius for post-processing smoothing, determining the size of the neighborhood used to average local values and reduce high-frequency detail. A radius of 0 disables smoothing.
post_smoothing_radius.label: Smoothing Radius

FillTalus.description: Fill the heightmap starting from the highest elevations using a regular downslope.

seed.description: Random seed number. The random seed is an offset to the randomized process. A different seed will produce a new result.
seed.label: Seed

FindCutPath.description: Generates a path between two domain boundaries by selecting start and end points using weighted sampling and connecting them with a midpoint-based subdivision.
FindCutPath.label: FindCutPath

favor_boundary_center.description: Biases selection toward the center of the boundary when randomly picking the start and end points.
favor_boundary_center.label: Favor Boundary Center

favor_lower_elevation.description: Biases selection toward lower values in the input field when randomly picking the start and end points.
favor_lower_elevation.label: Favor Lower Elevation

favor_sinks.description: Biases selection toward local minima (cells lower than or equal to their neighbors) when randomly picking the start and end points.
favor_sinks.label: Favor Sinks (Local Minima)

seed.description: Random seed number. The random seed is an offset to the randomized process. A different seed will produce a new result.

FlatbedCarve.description: Carves and blends a flatbed shape along a path into an existing heightmap using a smooth radial falloff. The operator is typically used to create river beds, channels, or flattened corridors that follow a user-defined path.
FlatbedCarve.label: FlatbedCarve

bottom_extent.description: Radius of the flatbed region measured from the path centerline, defining the half-width of the carved bed.
bottom_extent.label: Bed Half-Width

depth.description: Vertical depth of the bed carved below the surrounding terrain.
depth.label: Bed Depth

falloff_distance_ratio.description: Relative width of the smooth transition region outside the bed, expressed as a ratio of the bed half-width.
falloff_distance_ratio.label: Falloff Width Ratio

outer_slope.description: Linear slope applied beyond the falloff region to smoothly reconnect the bed to the surrounding terrain.

preserve_bedshape.description: Preserves the original bed profile when radial noise is applied, preventing distortion of the flatbed shape.
preserve_bedshape.label: Preserve Bed Shape

radial_profile.description: Radial profile function used to define the cross-sectional shape of the bed (e.g. smoothstep, linear).

radial_profile_parameter.description: Shape parameter controlling the curvature or sharpness of the selected radial profile.

vmin.description: Minimum height value assigned to the bed bottom, defining the base elevation of the carved region.

FloodingLakeSystem.description: Simulates lake formation on a terrain by filling topographic depressions. It applies a depression-filling method to determine the resulting water surface elevation.

GaborWaveFbm.label: GaborWaveFbm

angle.description: Controls the base orientation of the Gabor wavelets, influencing the dominant direction of the noise pattern. Expressed in degrees.

angle_spread_ratio.description: Determines how much the local angle of the Gabor kernel can vary. A low value results in straighter structures, while a high value introduces more directional variation.
angle_spread_ratio.label: angle_spread_ratio

lacunarity.description: The frequency scaling factor for successive noise octaves. Higher values increase the frequency of each successive octave.
lacunarity.label: Lacunarity

octaves.description: The number of octaves for fractal noise generation. More octaves add finer details to the terrain.
octaves.label: Octaves

persistence.description: The amplitude scaling factor for subsequent noise octaves. Lower values reduce the contribution of higher octaves.
persistence.label: Persistence

HydraulicParticle.description: HydraulicParticle is a particle-based hydraulic erosion operator that simulates the erosion and sediment transport processes that occur due to the flow of water over a terrain represented by the input heightmap. This type of operator models erosion by tracking the movement of virtual particles (or sediment particles) as they are transported by water flow and interact with the terrain. Erosion is gradient-driven: flat or masked-to-zero input has no slope and produces little or no change. Erode full-domain relief first, then multiply by the land mask.
HydraulicParticle.label: HydraulicParticle

The terrain is converted to a mesh, eroded through flow accumulation and slope-driven processes, then projected back to a heightmap. post_gain.description: Mid-centered gain transformation applied to the elevation values. This is a non-linear recurve operator centered around the mid elevation (typically 0.5). post_gain.label: Gain

post_gamma.description: Standard gamma correction applied to the elevation values. This is a monotonic power-law remapping that shifts emphasis toward low or high elevations, making the overall shape sharper or bulkier without changing its ordering.
post_gamma.label: Gamma

post_inverse.description: Inverts the output values after processing, flipping low and high values across the midrange.

post_remap.description: Linearly remaps the output values to a specified target range (default is [0, 1]).

post_saturate.description: Modifies the amplitude of elevations by first clamping them to a given interval and then scaling them so that the restricted interval matches the original input range. This enhances contrast in elevation variations while maintaining overall structure.
post_saturate.label: Saturation Range

post_smoothing_radius.description: Defines the radius for post-processing smoothing, determining the size of the neighborhood used to average local values and reduce high-frequency detail. A radius of 0 disables smoothing.
post_smoothing_radius.label: Smoothing Radius

seed.description: Random seed number. The random seed is an offset to the randomized process. A different seed will produce a new result.

weight.description: Controls how much higher FBM octaves contribute to the noise based on local elevation. post_saturate.description: Modifies the amplitude of elevations by first clamping them to a given interval and then scaling them so that the restricted interval matches the original input range. This enhances contrast in elevation variations while maintaining overall structure.

post_smoothing_radius.description: Defines the radius for post-processing smoothing, determining the size of the neighborhood used to average local values and reduce high-frequency detail. A radius of 0 disables smoothing.

k_depth_ratio.description: Controls how much snow becomes resistant to motion as depth increases. Higher values make thick snow more stable.

k_depth_slope_ratio.description: Increases the effective repose angle with snow depth, allowing deep snow to maintain steeper slopes.

k_melt_factor.description: Global multiplier for snow melting. Higher values cause snow to thin or disappear faster in melting areas.

k_snow.description: Controls the speed and intensity of snow avalanches when slopes exceed the repose angle.

talus_global.description: Base repose angle of snow. Higher values allow steeper slopes before snow starts to slide.

thermal_talus_ratio.description: Controls how strongly thermal creep depends on the repose angle. Lower values produce smoother snow on shallow slopes.

persistence.label: Persistence

post_gain.description: Mid-centered gain transformation applied to the elevation values. This is a non-linear recurve operator centered around the mid elevation (typically 0.5). post_gamma.description: Standard gamma correction applied to the elevation values. This is a monotonic power-law remapping that shifts emphasis toward low or high elevations, making the overall shape sharper or bulkier without changing its ordering.
post_gamma.label: Gamma

post_inverse.description: Inverts the output values after processing, flipping low and high values across the midrange.

post_remap.description: Linearly remaps the output values to a specified target range (default is [0, 1]).
post_remap.label: Remap Range

post_saturate.description: Modifies the amplitude of elevations by first clamping them to a given interval and then scaling them so that the restricted interval matches the original input range. This enhances contrast in elevation variations while maintaining overall structure.
post_saturate.label: Saturation Range

post_smoothing_radius.description: Defines the radius for post-processing smoothing, determining the size of the neighborhood used to average local values and reduce high-frequency detail. A radius of 0 disables smoothing.
post_smoothing_radius.label: Smoothing Radius

return_type.description: Defines the type of Voronoi information returned.

seed.description: Random seed number. The random seed is an offset to the randomized process. A different seed will produce a new result.
seed.label: Seed

weight.description: Controls how much higher FBM octaves contribute to the noise based on local elevation. WaterDepthDryOut.description: Reduces (dries out) the water depth by applying a ratio to the input depth. This can be used to simulate evaporation, infiltration, or partial drying of flooded areas. An optional mask can be provided to control where the drying effect is applied.
WaterDepthDryOut.label: WaterDepthDryOut

WaterDepthFromMask.description: Computes water depth over a terrain using a mask to define flooded regions. The method performs a harmonic interpolation (Laplace equation) over the masked domain using a Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR) solver. The resulting water surface is interpolated from boundary conditions, and the water depth is obtained as the difference between this surface and the terrain elevation.
WaterDepthFromMask.label: WaterDepthFromMask

iterations.description: Maximum number of SOR iterations used to solve the harmonic interpolation.
iterations.label: Max Iterations

mask_threshold.description: Threshold used to convert the input mask into a binary field. Values above the threshold define flooded regions, while lower values act as boundaries.
mask_threshold.label: Mask Activation Threshold

omega.description: Relaxation factor for the SOR solver. Values between 1 and 2 are recommended for faster convergence.
omega.label: Relaxation Factor

tolerance.description: Convergence tolerance. The solver stops when the maximum update between iterations falls below this value.
tolerance.label: Convergence Tolerance

water_depth.caption: water_depth
water_depth.description: Output water depth map representing flooded areas.

water_mask.caption: water_mask
water_mask.description: Input mask defining where water can accumulate. Values above the threshold indicate flooded regions.

WaterElevationFromDepth.description: Computes the absolute water elevation by adding the terrain elevation and the water depth. This simplifies workflows where only depth is available. The resulting water elevation can be used, for example, when exporting water as an asset with ExportAsset.
WaterElevationFromDepth.label: WaterElevationFromDepth

water_depth.caption: water_depth

water_elevation.caption: water_elevation
water_elevation.description: Output absolute water elevation computed as elevation + water_depth.

WaterMask.description: Computes a gradient-based water mask using an extended water-depth model. This produces a smooth mask indicating regions that become flooded when water depth is artificially increased by a specified amount. It can also be used to generate a transition mask between water and ground, useful for effects such as texturing a sand beach.

White.description: White noise operator generates a random signal with a flat power spectral density.
White.label: White

post_gain.description: Mid-centered gain transformation applied to the elevation values. This is a non-linear recurve operator centered around the mid elevation (typically 0.5). Increasing the gain pushes values toward the minimum and maximum elevations, creating flatter low/high regions with a steeper transition around the midpoint.
post_gain.label: Gain

post_gamma.description: Standard gamma correction applied to the elevation values. This is a monotonic power-law remapping that shifts emphasis toward low or high elevations, making the overall shape sharper or bulkier without changing its ordering.
post_gamma.label: Gamma

post_inverse.description: Inverts the output values after processing, flipping low and high values across the midrange.
post_inverse.label: Invert Output

post_mix.description: Mixing factor for blending input and output values. A value of 0 uses only the input, 1 uses only the output, and intermediate values perform a linear interpolation.
post_mix.label: Mix Factor

post_mix_method.description: Method used to combine input and output values. Options include linear interpolation (default), min, max, smooth min, smooth max, add, and subtract.
post_mix_method.label: Mix Method

post_remap.description: Linearly remaps the output values to a specified target range (default is [0, 1]).
post_remap.label: Remap Range

post_saturate.description: Modifies the amplitude of elevations by first clamping them to a given interval and then scaling them so that the restricted interval matches the original input range. This enhances contrast in elevation variations while maintaining overall structure.
post_saturate.label: Saturation Range

post_smoothing_radius.description: Defines the radius for post-processing smoothing, determining the size of the neighborhood used to average local values and reduce high-frequency detail. A radius of 0 disables smoothing.
post_smoothing_radius.label: Smoothing Radius

seed.description: Random seed number. The random seed is an offset to the randomized process. A different seed will produce a new result.
seed.label: Seed

dr.description: Displacement relative to the domain size (radial direction).

Zoom.description: Applies a zoom effect to an heightmap with an adjustable center. This function scales the input 2D array by a specified zoom factor, effectively resizing the array's contents. The zoom operation is centered around a specified point within the array, allowing for flexible zooming behavior.
Zoom.label: Zoom

center.description: Reference center within the heightmap. Coordinates are in domain units; center.y is measured from the bottom of the map (y increases upward).
center.label: center

periodic.description: If set to `true`, the zoom is periodic.
periodic.label: periodic

remap.description: Remap the operator's output to a specified range, defaulting to [0, 1].
remap.label: remap

zoom_factor.description: The factor by which to zoom the heightmap.
zoom_factor.label: zoom_factor

dx.caption: dx
dx.description: Displacement with respect to the domain size (x-direction).

dy.description: Displacement with respect to the domain size (y-direction).

input.caption: input
input.description: Displacement with respect to the domain size (x-direction).
